newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ord Minnett denies Fairfax selldown.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ord Minnett denies Fairfax selldown.

text.p: Australian broker Ord Minnett Securities Ltd said on Friday it was not involved in any selldown of Canadian media mogul Conrad Black's 25 percent stake in publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, contrary to some media reports.
"There is no selldown being done by us," said Ord Minnett Securities Director and Head of Institutional dealing, Chris Hutchinson.
"We are not doing anything for Conrad Black or Kerry Packer or anyone (on Fairfax) at this stage," Hutchinson told Reuters.

The Australian newspaper said in a report on Friday that Black was believed to be preparing to sell his Fairfax stake and that Black's Australian stockbroker, Ord Minnett, was understood to be making confidential soundings of fund managers to see if they were prepared to buy the shares.

Black's Hollinger International Inc said in April when bidding for the remaining 36 percent of Britain's The Telegraph Plc that Telegraph shareholders would be entitled to a further cash payment if the Telegraph's 25 percent stake in Fairfax was sold for more than A$3.00 a share net of tax within the next two years.
Black reaffirmed after that April announcement that he was committed to seeking a larger than 25 percent stake in Fairfax.

But he has also said he would quit his Fairfax stake if he was not allowed to increase his stake beyond 25 percent, arguing he is not in a strong enough position to fend off takeover offers from others like Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd.
PBL owns about 17 percent of Fairfax and News owns about five percent.

Black is currently restrained by foreign ownership rules from increasing his stake while Packer is prevented from buying a larger stake in Fairfax by cross media rules which stop the ownership of major television and newspapers in the same city.
The new conservative government has said it wants to conduct an inquiry into these rules later this year.

Many industry players expect the rules will be loosened, allowing ownership changes at large media companies like Fairfax, but the government has been careful not to indicate what the inquiry might find.
PBL said earlier this month it would prefer a merger of PBL and Fairfax if cross ownership rules were relaxed.
Fairfax share's were down four cents at A$2.64 by 10.55 am (0055 GMT).
